_comment_letters: A letter name that ENDS IN A CONSONANT must keep its halant: ଏମ୍ ଏନ୍ ଏସ୍ ଏଲ୍ ଏଫ୍ ଏଚ୍ ଆର୍. Odia PRONOUNCES the word-final inherent vowel (ରାମ is 'ramo', not 'ram'), so a halant-less ଏମ is read 'emo' and MOP came out as 'emo-o-pi' — reported as 'MO OP'. Letter names ending in a vowel (ଡି ଏ ପି କେ ଓ ଟି ୟୁ ଜି ସି) take no halant. The canonical spelling of every letter is _LETTER_NAMES in technical_terms.py — copy from there, do not retype by ear.
_comment_pairs: Add BOTH keys for a new acronym: the Latin one (MOP) and the Odia one the glossary rewrites it to (ଏମଓପି). apply_glossary runs first on the TTS path, so the Latin key alone is not enough.
